chunks: And fields of corn and date-palm trees with soft and tender spathes,
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the date palms and grain fields of the disbelievers in Surah Ash-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse highlights the agricultural prosperity of the Quraysh, specifically their cultivation of grain and date palms with tender, soft clusters (tal'uhu hadhim), serving as a tangible sign of divine provision. Shia exegetes often contextualize this within the broader theme of material blessings being a test of gratitude, contrasting the disbelievers' focus on worldly sustenance with their neglect of spiritual truth. The description of the 'soft' or 'crushed' spathes emphasizes the peak freshness of the dates, underscoring the immediacy and abundance of God's gifts to the people of Makkah.
